transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, your clinical conversational agent. I conducted your post-cataract surgery follow-up check and I'm here to answer any questions you may have about your recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for checking in. I do have a few questions. To start off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're interested in getting back to gardening. According to our guidelines, you can start with light exercise, such as gardening, about 1 week after surgery. Just remember to be gentle and take care of your eyes. Also, be careful not to get any water in your eyes. Do you have any other questions about gardening or exercise after surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information! That helps a lot. I also wanted to know, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're referring to eye drops for dry eyes. You should continue to use them as prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. And if you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma, or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Do you have any other questions about your eye drops or dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That clarifies things, thank you. Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Mild sensitivity to bright light is normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. We recommend wearing sunglasses when you're going outside to help with this. However, if you're experiencing significant pain or your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further. Does that make sense?
transcript.delivered: Mild sensitivity to bright light is normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. We recommend wearing sunglasses when you're going outside to help with this.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. If it's been more than a week, you can also consider visiting your optician to get a new glasses prescription, approximately 6 weeks after surgery. Do you have any other questions about your vision or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that covers all my concerns. Thanks for all the information, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! I'm glad I could help. If you have any more questions or concerns in the future, don't hesitate to reach out. Otherwise, I'll just confirm that I've answered all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery. Is that correct?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that's correct. Thank you again for your help!

verdict.label: fail
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` in turn 6 by stating, "Mild sensitivity to bright light is normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses." It also conveyed `mild_case_advice` in the same turn by recommending, "We recommend wearing sunglasses when you're going outside to help with this." However, the `escalation_criteria` point was not conveyed at all, as the agent was interrupted before it could deliver any information about red-flag symptoms.
